html:
The Massawomeck were an Iroquoian people who lived around the headwaters of the Potomac, Monongahela and Youghiogheny rivers, in what is now western Maryland and the eastern panhandle of West Virginia, in the early 1600s.

Almost all that is known of them comes from Captain John Smith of Jamestown, who met a war party of theirs in bark canoes on Chesapeake Bay in 1608. The Powhatan and the Piscataway feared them as raiders. Who they were is uncertain: they may have been an Iroquoian group later destroyed or absorbed by the Haudenosaunee, or possibly related to the Erie. They disappear from the records after the 1630s.
